slides.title:
SD-WAN didn't remove
the WAN engineer.
It moved the *hard part*.
slides.body: Configuring links used to be the work.

slides.title: What that work was
slides.body:
Two circuits.
A routing protocol.
A failover design you could draw.

slides.title: Now
slides.body:
That part is largely *solved*.
The vendors aren't wrong
when they say so.

slides.title: What replaced it
slides.body:
What does *"good"* mean
for this application?

slides.title: Replication
slides.body:
Takes whatever is left.
Competes with *neither*.

slides.title: The catch
slides.body:
Those aren't network facts.
They're *business decisions*
about which application loses.

slides.title: Where it stalls
steps: In a meeting, not a lab.
Which is the same as *nobody* answering.

slides.title:
The *classification*
is the deliverable.
slides.body:
The overlay is just
what enforces it.

Follow *@mzsnetworks*
